## Simple explanation

A validation set is practice feedback for a model developer: it helps compare
candidate models and settings without using the final exam, the test set.

## Technical explanation

The validation set is a portion of labeled data kept separate from parameter
fitting. Developers use its metrics to select architectures, tune
hyperparameters, choose decision thresholds, or apply early stopping. Repeated
adaptation to validation results can overfit the validation set, so it is not
an unbiased final estimate of generalization.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Validation results influence many development decisions. A clean split makes
those decisions measurable while keeping final evaluation independent.
Time-dependent, grouped, or user-level data may require structured splits to
prevent leakage between training and validation.

## How it works

Split data according to the deployment setting, fit parameters on the training
portion, and evaluate candidates on validation data. Freeze the chosen pipeline
before measuring it on a separate test set. In cross-validation, several
training/validation folds are used to make model selection less dependent on
one split.

## Practical example

For next-month demand prediction, train on earlier periods and validate on a
later period. Compare candidate models on the later period, then reserve a still
later test period for final reporting.

## Common misconceptions

- The validation set is not interchangeable with the test set; using test
  results to make iterative choices contaminates the final estimate.
- A random split is not always appropriate. Related records from the same
  person or future observations can leak information across partitions.
